text:
max: hitting truncated responses for long generations. client is configured with timeout=300 but requests still fail after ~60s with ReadTimeout. stack trace below, happened on v0.8.1

steph_support: sorry about that — can you paste a minimal repro and mention if you're using streaming?

max: here's the simplified snippet — it's sync requests, using the python SDK Client(timeout=300) and stream=True
```
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key='x', timeout=300)
resp = client.generate(model='rw-large', prompt='very long...', stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
```

max: error log: requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout: HTTPConnectionPool(host='api.redwood.ai', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=60)

matt_devex: two likely causes: 1) env var is overriding client arg, 2) SDK expects timeout in seconds but an env var is in ms. which env vars do you have set?

max: i checked, REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 in our environment, but i thought client param should override env?

steph_support: historically client args win, but there was a subtle change in 0.8.x where we read legacy env var first for compatibility. also the requests adapter uses a per-socket read timeout default of 60s unless explicitly passed as a tuple (connect, read). passing single float sets both in requests normally, but our wrapper may be feeding it into urllib3 incorrectly.

jane_ops: also note streaming endpoints are sensitive to read timeouts — if the client read timeout is shorter than server chunk interval, connection will cut. many teams saw truncation when server emits keepalives every 70s.

max: ah ok. is there a workaround? i can't change env across our CI easily right now.

matt_devex: quick workarounds:
- unset REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS or set to 300000
- pass timeout=(10, 300) explicitly to Client so connect/read are clear
- set retries=0 on the client to avoid retry wrappers masking timeouts

steph_support: can you try this patched snippet?
```
client = Client(api_key='x', timeout=(10, 300), retries=0)
resp = client.generate(..., stream=True)
```

max: tried that — now the ReadTimeout shows read timeout=300, streaming stayed open longer, but we still saw occasional early cutoff after ~260s.

matt_devex: that suggests another layer: our SDK maintains an internal per-chunk poll deadline of 270s for streaming to guard resources. in 0.8.1 that was hard-coded. newer SDKs expose chunk_timeout config.

max: which version fixes it?

matt_devex: upgrade to 0.9.0 — it adds two things: honors client-level tuple timeout correctly for the requests adapter, and exposes stream_chunk_timeout and environment var REDWOOD_STREAM_TIMEOUT_MS.

max: ok, any risks to upgrade? we pin a lot of deps.

steph_support: release notes for 0.9.0 are small; main breaking change is the env var rename (legacy still supported but priority changed). we tested on us-east for long gen and it resolved truncation.

eng_runtime: chiming in — we also saw users set REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS in deploy manifests thinking it's total generation timeout. it's actually used for non-streaming default in older SDKs. we should update docs to avoid ms/seconds confusion and add validation warnings when both client arg and env var conflict. filing a docs task.

deploy_bot: deploy:config-check succeeded for support/doc-fix branch (CI #3421)

max: thanks, upgrading to 0.9.0 + explicit timeout tuple fixed our case. marking resolved for now.

jane_ops: followup note for ops: if you rely on infra-level load balancer idle timeouts, ensure LB idle > stream_chunk_timeout + headroom, otherwise LB will sever connection even if client/server agree.

matt_devex: logging action items: 1) docs clarifying env var names and units; 2) add config validation warning when REDWOOD_TIMEOUT_MS present and client.timeout set; 3) consider making streaming default chunk_timeout larger.

max: appreciated. leaving logs here in case others hit this. :thumbsup:
